title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization
rationale: Already downloaded as P044. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes
rationale: Useful if historical hidden-state probing remains in the manuscript; existing P016 already covers probe controls.

title: Causal Inference in Natural Language Processing: Estimation, Prediction, Interpretation and Beyond
rationale: Corrects the old manuscript conflation of predictive adjustment and causal identification; covers text as treatment, outcome and confounding information. Useful across the historical policy experiment and observational readiness study.
abstract_summary: The survey organizes causal estimation and causal uses in NLP, including text as treatment, outcome or adjustment information, and distinguishes estimation from prediction and interpretation.

title: The Rise of AI Search: Implications for Information Markets and Human Judgement at Scale
rationale: Broad AI-search context; less urgent than direct GEO and attribution comparisons.

title: Estimating Causal Effects with Double Machine Learning -- A Method Evaluation
rationale: Useful applied DML robustness reading after the estimand and sampling unit are fixed; P090 and the new sensitivity paper take precedence.

title: DoubleML -- An Object-Oriented Implementation of Double Machine Learning in Python
rationale: The actual legacy estimator uses DoubleML and custom PLR residualization. Read implementation/estimand distinctions before interpreting binary-outcome coefficients or standard errors.
abstract_summary: DoubleML implements orthogonal-score and cross-fitting estimators for several causal models in Python, with extensible model specifications and nuisance learners.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
rationale: Feed-forward key-value interpretation does not validate the old layer-specific causal narrative; no current mechanistic intervention depends on it.

title: E-GEO: A Testbed for Generative Engine Optimization in E-Commerce
rationale: Already downloaded as P050. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: A Causal Information-Flow Framework for Unbiased Learning-to-Rank
rationale: Unbiased learning-to-rank is adjacent, but its exposure/feedback estimand should not be conflated with page-feature DML or source-support grading.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
rationale: Archive reference for old Llama 3 analysis; current V2 Llama 4 needs its own exact model provenance.

title: MS MARCO: A Human Generated MAchine Reading COmprehension Dataset
rationale: MS MARCO is background to other rankers, not the current frozen prompt/SERP dataset.

title: Generative Engine Optimization: How to Dominate AI Search
rationale: Already downloaded as P047. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: DoubleMLDeep: Estimation of Causal Effects with Multimodal Data
rationale: Multimodal nuisance estimation is not an implemented requirement of the current readiness/support analysis.

title: CC-GSEO-Bench: A Content-Centric Benchmark for Measuring Source Influence in Generative Search Engines
rationale: Direct novelty comparator: source influence across diverse intents and follow-up questions, with Exposure, Faithful Credit and Causal Impact separated. Read its operational definitions before claiming a new ideal-versus-realized source gap.
abstract_summary: CC-GSEO-Bench organizes over 1,000 articles and over 5,000 query-article pairs and evaluates article-level exposure, faithful credit and causal impact across query clusters.

title: Aligning Language Models with Observational Data: Opportunities and Risks from a Causal Perspective
rationale: Old appendix proposes reward/distillation work that is outside the current experiment.

title: Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Treatment and Causal Parameters
rationale: Already downloaded as P090. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: Zero-Shot Listwise Document Reranking with a Large Language Model
rationale: Historical listwise reranking comparator; P041 and P043 already cover the main lineage.

title: Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI
rationale: Useful broad reference, but a book download adds less immediate value than the focused identification and sensitivity sources.

title: RankVicuna: Zero-Shot Listwise Document Reranking with Open-Source Large Language Models
rationale: Useful only for a fuller history of open listwise rankers; current methods are bounded answer-generation/search loops.

title: TREC Deep Learning Track: Reusable Test Collections in the Large Data Regime
rationale: TREC collection background is already available through relevant reranking articles; current experiment does not use this collection.

title: RankZephyr: Effective and Robust Zero-Shot Listwise Reranking is a Breeze!

title: Do Large Language Models Favor Recent Content? A Study on Recency Bias in LLM-Based Reranking
rationale: Old manuscript section 2 calls this consistent with its freshness-demotion result, but the verified abstract reports promotion after artificial fresh-date injection. Essential to correct that comparison and distinguish intervention from observed freshness.
abstract_summary: The study injects artificial publication dates into TREC passages and finds newer passages promoted across seven reranking models, with listwise and pairwise preference changes.

title: Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting
rationale: Already downloaded as P045. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: Qwen2.5 Technical Report
rationale: Historical Qwen2.5 provenance; do not substitute for the exact current Qwen3.8 model documentation.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
rationale: Useful for the historical topical-competence feature; current readiness geometry uses LLM2Vec, already P024.

title: Debiasing Reward Models via Causally Motivated Inference-Time Intervention
rationale: Reward-model intervention supports an old future-work suggestion, not implemented source-importance measurement.

title: Is ChatGPT Good at Search? Investigating Large Language Models as Re-Ranking Agents
rationale: Already downloaded as P041. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: BERT Rediscovers the Classical NLP Pipeline
rationale: BERT layer analysis cannot establish when an autoregressive reranker causally commits to an admission decision.

title: BEIR: A Heterogenous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
rationale: Already downloaded as P056. Retain and read the existing copy; no duplicate retrieval is needed.

title: What Generative Search Engines Like and How to Optimize Web Content Cooperatively
rationale: AutoGEO is a direct content-preference and source-visibility comparator. Compare its content rewrites and learned preferences with measured readiness and fixed-source support judgments.
abstract_summary: AutoGEO extracts generative-engine preference rules, uses them in prompt-based rewriting and model training, and evaluates content traction alongside search utility.

title: Rank-R1: Enhancing Reasoning in LLM-based Document Rerankers via Reinforcement Learning
rationale: Useful reranking comparator if retaining a reranker survey; RL optimization is not part of current V2.

title: Causal alignment: Augmenting language models with A/B tests
rationale: Old future-work reference; A/B-driven alignment is not the implemented V2 outcome or judge.

title: Deep neural networks for estimation and inference
rationale: Additional asymptotic background; not required to justify the existing LightGBM estimator beyond P090.

title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
rationale: Already downloaded. Essential existing reading if keeping claims about probing and causal use.

title: Stepwise multiple testing as formalized data snooping
rationale: Read if retaining the old Romano-Wolf claims or adopting that correction; does not fix dependence or selection bias.

title: A setwise approach for effective and highly efficient zero-shot ranking with large language models
rationale: Completes historical reranker taxonomy; lower priority than source attribution and construct validation.

title: Correctness is not Faithfulness in RAG Attributions
rationale: Separates citation support/correctness from whether the model actually relied on a source. This is the central interpretive boundary for SI-v4 and the proposed source-gap outcome.
abstract_summary: The authors distinguish citation correctness from faithfulness and test post-rationalization, where a citation supports a statement without reflecting the model's actual use of the document.

title: Long Story Short: Omitted Variable Bias in Causal Machine Learning
rationale: Gives omitted-variable sensitivity bounds for flexible causal models, including partial linearity. Better matched to legacy PLR page-feature estimates than treating risk-ratio E-values as a universal sensitivity solution.
abstract_summary: The paper derives omitted-variable-bias bounds for several causal parameters using assumptions about omitted explanatory power and supplies machine-learning-compatible inference for those bounds.

title: Prediction-Powered Inference
rationale: Provides a route from a genuine independent human-labeled calibration sample plus machine predictions to uncertainty-aware population estimation. ARES P083 already applies this idea to RAG; the foundational method is missing. It is not automatic validation of SI-v4 or clustered ordinal rankings.
abstract_summary: Prediction-powered inference combines labeled observations with machine predictions to estimate quantities such as means and regression coefficients with confidence intervals while correcting prediction error.

title: Making Sense of Sensitivity: Extending Omitted Variable Bias
rationale: Clear regression sensitivity exposition. Useful companion to Long Story Short, but the latter is the more direct first download for flexible DML.
evidence: Crossref title/authors/DOI verified 2026-10-01; online date 2019-12-17, journal issue 2020.

title: Construct validity in psychological tests.
rationale: Read for a defensible readiness construct: agreement with model labels and a stable embedding direction do not by themselves establish construct validity.

title: Inside the search process: Information seeking from the user's perspective
rationale: Useful process-level search-intent background; downloaded Broder P006 and Jansen P013 cover a defensible first-pass intent foundation.

title: Effects of Deliberative and Implemental Mindsets on Persistence in Goal-Directed Behavior
rationale: Additional mindset/process background adds little to the already downloaded foundational intention literature for this prompt-text construct. Defer retrieval.

title: The Effects of Mindset on Behavior: Self-Regulation in Deliberative and Implemental Frames of Mind
rationale: Additional mindset/process background adds little to the already downloaded foundational intention literature for this prompt-text construct. Defer retrieval.

title: Exploratory search
rationale: Useful to prevent equating information seeking with low-quality or incomplete decision making; enriches the low-readiness end.

title: How do implementation intentions promote goal attainment? A test of component processes
rationale: Additional mindset/process background adds little to the already downloaded foundational intention literature for this prompt-text construct. Defer retrieval.

title: The Role of Deliberative Versus Implemental Mindsets in Time Prediction and Task Accomplishment
rationale: Additional mindset/process background adds little to the already downloaded foundational intention literature for this prompt-text construct. Defer retrieval.

title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
rationale: Useful probing survey, but P016 is already downloaded and the current main analysis is not a probe study.

title: Convergent and discriminant validation by the multitrait-multimethod matrix.
rationale: Read for convergent and discriminant validation. Agreement between Qwen and Mistral embeddings is insufficient if both follow lexical or genre shortcuts.

title: A Generalized Solution of the Orthogonal Procrustes Problem
rationale: Original Procrustes reference for the implemented alignment; helpful citation, lower priority than proving out-of-sample construct validity.

title: Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures (with comments and a rejoinder by the author)
rationale: Broad predictive-versus-explanatory modeling essay; focused DML and text-causal references address the present inferential problem more directly.

title: Measurement invariance conventions and reporting: The state of the art and future directions for psychological research
rationale: Practical measurement-invariance guide, useful after specifying generator, genre, topic and contract groups; P029 is already available.

title: Automatic Document Editing for Improved Ranking
rationale: Relevant document-editing comparator if the paper makes optimization claims, but V2 is currently measurement rather than a tested editing system.

title: Position: On the Risks of Generative Engine Optimization in the Era of LLMs
rationale: Useful ethical context, lower priority than methodological sources and direct empirical comparators.

title: Weighted kappa: Nominal scale agreement provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit.
rationale: Read for ordinal judge agreement and weighted disagreement; SI-v4 grades are ordered, not percentages or interval measurements. Prespecify weights and report class marginals.

title: Intraclass correlations: Uses in assessing rater reliability.
rationale: Use only after choosing a reliability model appropriate for ordinal ratings and the rater design; weighted kappa is the first retrieval priority.
